subsystems.name: Core Formatting
subsystems.description: This subsystem is the public, header-only formatting engine of {fmt}: it defines argument storage, parsing, and output primitives on which every other fmt feature builds. It is separated from src implementation files so that the template-heavy API can be instantiated in user code without requiring a compiled library core, and so that optional domains (chrono, color, printf, ranges, std types) can be included independently. Control flow starts with a format string and argument pack: dynamic_arg_list (include/fmt/args.h:43) owns copied arguments, basic_format_arg (include/fmt/base.h:2464) and value (include/fmt/base.h:2148) type-erase them, parse_context (include/fmt/base.h:842) walks the replacement fields, and compiled strings cut that walk short via compile_format_string (include/fmt/compile.h:385). The formatted output is written through buffer and iterator_buffer (include/fmt/base.h:1975) or through file and console wrappers in os.h and format-inl.h. Neighbouring subsystems are not listed in related_files for this cluster, but in practice this subsystem is the API consumed by the Core Library Implementation cluster and the C API implementation. It also provides the formatter extension points that ranges.h, std.h, chrono.h, and color.h specialize.

subsystems.name: Core Library Implementation
subsystems.description: This cluster is the compiled implementation part of {fmt}: src/fmt.cc, src/format.cc and src/os.cc provide the non-header definitions that make the library linkable as a real library, while test/posix-mock-test.cc and test/posix-mock.h exercise the POSIX layer with mocked system calls. It exists separately because the bulk of fmt is template code that must be header-only, but a small set of functions with external linkage (especially OS and locale/file operations) needs a translation unit and a module entry point. Data flows from the public headers into src/os.cc system_message and buffered_file implementations when formatting writes to files or consoles; src/fmt.cc establishes the FMT_MODULE export boundary; src/format.cc instantiates the core. The POSIX mock tests define scoped_mock and replacement open/close/read/write syscalls to verify src/os.cc behavior without real descriptors. The cluster connects to test/gtest-extra.h for its gtest support, and it is the compiled counterpart of the Core Formatting cluster.

subsystems.name: Documentation JavaScript
subsystems.description: This subsystem is the JavaScript supporting the documentation site for {fmt}. It is a small standalone script (doc/fmt.js) with no scanned functions, which suggests it wires up client-side behaviour such as search, navigation, or mobile menus that cannot be expressed in the generated static HTML. It exists as its own cluster because documentation assets have a completely different language, build process, and maintenance path from the C++ library. Data flow is trivial: the browser loads the script, and it manipulates the Document Object Model of the rendered documentation pages. No concrete symbols were extracted from the scanner, so the page-level description is intentionally high-level. The cluster has an empty related_files list, so it has no recorded coupling to the C++ clusters and can be changed independently.

subsystems.name: C API Header
subsystems.description: This subsystem is the C API header for {fmt}, exposing formatting entry points to C consumers. It exists to give non-C++ programs a stable ABI: instead of templates, it defines FMT_CAPI macros for symbol export and a set of fmt_from_* converters that translate C scalar and string values into the library's internal argument representation. Data flows from user C code through those converters (fmt_from_int at include/fmt/fmt-c.h:76, fmt_from_str at include/fmt/fmt-c.h:104, fmt_from_ptr at include/fmt/fmt-c.h:108) into the implementation in src/fmt-c.cc for formatting. The header's related_files list is empty, but logically it is the C-facing counterpart of the Core Formatting subsystem, sharing only the functions declared here rather than C++ templates.

Its central function convert_c_format_args (src/fmt-c.cc:14) bridges C values into fmt::format_args, after which fmt_vformat (src/fmt-c.cc:38) and fmt_vprint (src/fmt-c.cc:54) perform the actual formatting and printing. subsystems.name: CLI Argument Parser
subsystems.description: support/docopt.py is a vendored copy of the docopt command-line argument parser. It exists as a separate subsystem so the project can parse `usage:`-style help strings into a declarative pattern tree without adding a third-party dependency or coupling parsing to application modules. Control flow begins with docopt() at support/docopt.py:490, which parses the usage message via parse_seq, parse_expr, and parse_atom, then matches the user's argv through parse_argv and the Pattern match chain; transform, fix_identities, and fix_repeating_arguments normalize the parsed pattern before matching. Options and flags are represented by the Option and Argument leaf classes, while Required, Optional, OneOrMore, and Either compose them into a pattern tree at support/docopt.py:219 and support/docopt.py:268. The item's related_files list is empty, so this module is self-contained and communicates with the rest of the repository only by returning a dict from docopt().

subsystems.name: Character Data Generator
subsystems.description: support/printable.py is a code-generation utility that emits a compact representation of the printable Unicode codepoint set. It exists as a separate subsystem because generating this derived table at build time keeps the table readable and lets the generator run independently from the runtime code that consumes it. main() at support/printable.py:133 loads a file through get_file(), enumerates Unicode codepoints with get_codepoints(), converts the set to ranges with to_ranges(), and then prints either compressed ranges via compress_normal() and compress_singletons() or escaped literals via get_escaped(), print_singletons(), and print_normal(). The NUM_CODEPOINTS and Codepoint constants define the iteration bounds and item shape used throughout. Its related_files list is empty, so this script is standalone; its output is intended to be checked in and consumed by other subsystems as static Python data.

subsystems.name: C++ Documentation Handler
subsystems.description: support/python/mkdocstrings_handlers/cxx/__init__.py is a mkdocstrings handler that renders C++ API documentation from Doxygen XML. It is isolated as its own subsystem because mkdocstrings needs a per-language plugin entry point, and keeping the C++ converter separate prevents XML/Doxygen concerns from leaking into Python doc machinery. get_handler() at support/python/mkdocstrings_handlers/cxx/__init__.py:447 returns a CxxHandler instance; the handler's __init__ at line 236 stores configuration, collect() at line 358 walks Doxygen compound nodes into Definition objects, and render() at line 423 converts them to HTML by delegating to render_decl() at line 181 and the convert_* helpers such as convert_node, convert_type, convert_params, convert_return_type, and convert_template_params. tag_map and tag_text_map drive XML-to-HTML tag conversion, and escape_html sanitizes text at line 63. The related_files list is empty, meaning this plugin is self-contained; mkdocstrings discovers it through get_handler() when the handler name is requested.

subsystems.name: Release Automation
subsystems.description: support/release.py automates the git and environment steps needed to produce a release. It exists separately so release orchestration is scriptable and repeatable rather than being embedded in CI configuration or in library code. Runner is a thin command wrapper whose __call__() at support/release.py:74 executes shell commands, while Git at support/release.py:19 wraps common git operations such as clone, fetch, checkout, commit, push, reset, and update by mapping each method to a git invocation through call(). clean_checkout() at line 60 prepares a clean tree, and create_build_env() at line 81 with create_doc_env() at line 92 construct Env subprocess environments for building and documentation. The related_files list is empty, so this is a standalone operational script rather than an imported application module.

overview.description: The repository is {fmt}, a C++ formatting library whose runtime behavior is built on the header-only Core Formatting engine, complemented by the Core Library Implementation for compiled OS/file/locale operations. The C API Header and C API Implementation expose a stable ABI to C consumers by converting C values into the core's C++ argument representation. The remaining subsystems are independent supporting tools: Documentation JavaScript enhances the site, CLI Argument Parser and Character Data Generator are standalone Python utilities, C++ Documentation Handler renders Doxygen XML for mkdocstrings, and Release Automation scripts the release process.
